QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_37

question.text: An AIF reports PIC = 0.90 in its quarterly LP letter. What does this indicate?

answer.text: The fund is about to complete its final close
The fund has drawn down most of its capital commitments from LPs
The fund has 90% recovery rate on its investments
The fund has only 10% NPA exposure

explanation.text: The Logic: PIC = Paid-In / Committed = 0.90 means 90% of committed capital has been called down. This signals the fund is near the end of its drawdown / investment phase. The same answer is keyed in the workbook's sample question on this metric. The Trap: Option A confuses drawdown with fund-raising. Option D is a credit metric, not PIC. Option C conflates PIC with DPI. Note: The PIC interpretation is taken from the fund performance chapter and is reinforced by the workbook's sample question.
